Short answer: Choose the system that supports your real bookkeeping, tax, payroll, inventory, payment, reporting, and accountant workflow. A cheaper plan is not cheaper if the books need rebuilding.

What this means for your business

Accounting software is a record system, not just an invoice template. Your business type, sales tax, payroll, inventory, entities, bank feeds, and professional support change the fit.

What to watch

  • Choosing before asking the person who closes the books or files taxes.
  • Features assumed from an old plan comparison.
  • Historical records with no clean export.
  • Payment, payroll, or bank-feed fees left out of total cost.

Do this next

  1. Ask the bookkeeper or accountant which records and reports they require.
  2. List payroll, inventory, sales tax, projects, payments, and users.
  3. Compare current official plans and total fees.
  4. Test export, reconciliation, and year-end handoff before migrating.

When Little Fight fits

We can connect the business workflow around the accounting system. Accounting and tax decisions belong with a qualified accountant or bookkeeper.
